{{Socialism in Belarus}}'''Stanislav Stanislavovich Shushkevich'''{{efn|{{langx|be|Станіслаў Станіслававіч Шушкевіч|translit=Stanislaŭ Stanislavavič Šuškievič}}; {{langx|ru|Станислав Станиславович Шушкевич|translit=Stanislav Stanislavovich Shushkevich}}; {{langx|pl|Stanisław Szuszkiewicz}}}} (15 December 1934 – 3 May 2022) was a Belarusian politician and scientist who served as the first [[head of state]] of independent Belarus after it [[dissolution of the Soviet Union|seceded]] from the [[Soviet Union]], serving as the first [[Supreme Council of Belarus#Chairmen of the Supreme Soviet|chairman of the Supreme Soviet]] (also called chairman of Parliament or president) from 1991 to 1994. He supported [[social democratic]] reforms and played a key role in the creation of the [[Commonwealth of Independent States]]. He later became an [[Belarusian opposition|opposition]] leader against [[Alexander Lukashenko]].

As a scientist, he was a [[corresponding member]] of the [[Belarusian Academy of Sciences]], [[Doktor nauk|Doctor]] in Physics and Mathematics, recipient of various state awards, professor and the author and originator of textbooks and over 150 articles and 50 inventions.

== Early life and education ==
[[File:Stanisłaŭ Šuškievič. Станіслаў Шушкевіч (1926).jpg|thumb|left|Shushkevich's father, Stanislav Petrovich Shushkevich, pictured sometime before 1926.]]
Stanislav Stanislavovich Shushkevich was born on 15 December 1934 in the city of [[Minsk]], in what was then part of the [[Byelorussian SSR]], to a family of teachers. Stanislav's father, {{ill|Stanislav Petrovich Shushkevich|ru|Шушкевич, Станислав Петрович}}, was a poet who briefly wrote for the newspapers ''Literature and Art'', ''Chyrvonaya Zmena'', and ''Zvyazda'' before being repressed during the [[Great Purge]] in 1936 and sent into exile in the Russian SFSR.<ref name="father">{{cite book |title=Беларускія пісьменнікі: Біябібліяграфічны слоўнік |date=1995 |publisher=Беларуская Энцыклапедыя імя Петруся Броўкі |volume=6|location=Minsk |pages=398-399 |url=https://archive.org/details/bel-enc-pism/Bielaruskija_pismienniki_6_6/page/397/mode/2up?q=%D0%A8%D1%83%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D1%96%D1%87 |access-date=24 October 2026|language=be}}</ref> He returned to Byelorussia in 1946 after serving his sentence, before being repressed again in 1949 and sent to the [[Krasnoyarsk Krai]], returning to Minsk only in 1956.<ref name="father" /> He was fully [[Political rehabilitation|rehabilitated]] in both cases in 1975.<ref name="father" /> Stanislav's mother, {{ill|Helena Romanowska|ru|Романовская, Елена Людвиковна}}, was an ethnic Pole of [[szlachta]] (noble) origin who was also a writer before her husband's arrest in 1936, which forced her to leave writing and become a teacher in various schools in Minsk.<ref>{{cite web |title=Helena Romanowska |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829033131/https://www.ipsb.nina.gov.pl/a/biografia/helena-romanowska |website=www.ipsb.nina.gov.pl |access-date=24 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Беларускія пісьменнікі: Біябібліяграфічны слоўнік |date=1995 |publisher=Беларуская Энцыклапедыя імя Петруся Броўкі |volume=5 |location=Minsk |pages=149-150 |url=https://archive.org/details/bel-enc-pism/Bielaruskija_pismienniki_6_6/page/397/mode/2up?q=%D0%A8%D1%83%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D1%96%D1%87 |access-date=24 October 2026|language=be}}</ref>

Shushkevich would end up growing up on Slepianskaya Street, which was part of the Komarovka district in Minsk.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=29-30}} Due to his father's arrest, his mother attempted to make sure that Shushkevich would not pursue [[humanities]], and also taught him both the Belarusian and Russian languages.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=11-12,37}} Shushkevich's childhood would then be significantly affected by [[World War II]] and the [[German occupation of Byelorussia during World War II|German occupation of Byelorussia]]. His family initially attempted to flee east to the Russian SFSR after the start of [[Operation Barbarossa]], but could not do so due to the highways being damaged by the Germans near [[Barysaw]], so they returned back to Minsk.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=32-33}} Upon returning, Stanislav moved to live with his grandfather, Pyotr, in a village just outside of Minsk, together with his mother and grandmother.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=9-10,33}}<ref name="sva1">{{cite news |last1=Навумчык |first1=Сяргей |title=Памёр першы кіраўнік незалежнай Беларусі Станіслаў Шушкевіч. Шлях асобы і палітыка |url=https://www.svaboda.org/a/31822342.html |access-date=24 October 2026 |work=Радыё Свабода |date=17 May 2022 |language=be}}</ref> Later, a [[Jewish]] boy was resettled into the house, and although they risked [[execution]], none of the neighbours on the street informed anyone about the boy.<ref name="sva1" />{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=33-34}} After the [[Minsk offensive]] and the liberation of the city, Shushkevich, who had previously been [[homeschooled]] due to the war, returned to secondary school.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=37,40-43}} He graduated in 1951 with a silver medal<ref name="sva1" /> after also having attended the young pioneer camp, [[Artek (camp)|Artek]], in Crimea, due to the articles he had written for a local pioneer newspaper.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=37,40-43}} 

After graduation, he attempted to enter the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics at the [[Belarusian State University]]. According to Shushkevich in his memoir, although medalists normally did not take exams, he was required to take multiple exams because they did not want to take the son of somebody who had been repressed recently in 1949.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=44-45}} However, after getting in, Shushkevich joined the [[Komsomol]], the youth division of the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] (CPSU), and became its organiser for his course while also working part-time at pioneer camps and [[tutoring]].{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=48-54}} Shushkevich then decided to pursue graduate education, enrolling at the Institute of Physics of the [[Belarusian Academy of Sciences]]. During his graduate studies, he worked in the laboratory of {{ill|Mikhail Yelyashevich|ru|Ельяшевич, Михаил Александрович}}, a renowned Belarusian physicist who authored the [[monograph]] ''Molecular Spectroscopy''.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=55-57}} In 1959, Shushkevich completed graduate school, but did not yet finish his [[dissertation]], instead opting to take time off.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=14}} He returned a few years later to finish his dissertation, this time at his alma mater, the Belarusian State University, in its newly founded Department of Nuclear Physics and the Peaceful Use of Atomic Energy under Alexander Pisarevsky, who had been invited from the [[Saint Petersburg Electrotechnical University]].<ref name="novy" /> In 1963, Shushkevich defended his [[Candidate of Sciences]] thesis, which was within the developing field of [[radio electronics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Шушкевич Станислав Станиславович |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116174937/http://www.physics.bsu.by/ru/node/608 |website=web.archive.org |access-date=24 October 2026}}</ref> His dissertation's working product, a probing radio-frequency signal, was funded by a research institute of the KGB.<ref name="novy" />

== Academic career ==
[[File:OSWALD'S APARTMENT BUILDING - MINSK - BELARUS.jpg|thumb|left|[[Lee Harvey Oswald]]'s apartment in Minsk. In 1960, Shushkevich gave Oswald lessons in the Russian language, before returning to complete his Candidate of Sciences.]]
=== Early work at the Minsk Radio Plant (1959-1961) ===
After temporarily taking time off from graduate school in 1959, he initially worked as a junior researcher at the school.<ref name="bulvar">{{cite news |title=«Экс-председатель Верховного Совета Беларуси Станислав ШУШКЕВИЧ: «После 20-летней отсидки советскую власть мой отец любил совершенно безумно» |url=https://bulvar.com.ua/gazeta/archive/s38_66871/8771.html |access-date=24 October 2026 |work=bulvar.com.ua |date=23 September 2014}}</ref> Due to the low pay, he took up a job in 1960 working at the Special Design Bureau of the Minsk Radio Plant, where he had previously obtained an [[internship]].<ref name="bulvar" /> He worked at the plant for a little over a year, developing instruments he had been working on during his graduate studies, including a select [[amplifier]] and synchronous [[detector]] that were later developed and produced at a plant in [[Murom]] for twenty years.<ref name="19november" /><ref name="novy">{{cite news |last1=Тамковіч |first1=Аляксандр |title=Станіслаў Шушкевіч: «Нікога з сяброў я не страціў, таму што нікому не здрадзіў» |url=https://novychas.online/asoba/perszamu-kirauniku-nezaleznaj-belarusi-86? |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=Новы Час |date=4 May 2022 |language=be}}</ref>

While working at the plant, the party secretary, Libezin, gave Shushkevich a party errand: teach [[Lee Harvey Oswald]], a newly arrived American to Minsk who was working at the plant as a metalworker, the Russian language.<ref name="mail">{{cite book |last1=Mailer |first1=Norman |title=Oswald's Tale: An American Mystery |date=23 January 2007 |publisher=Random House Publishing Group |isbn=978-1-58836-593-4 |pages=81-83 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Oswald_s_Tale/WSKKEJXZs_oC?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=Shushkevich |access-date=25 October 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Shushkevich agreed and taught Oswald in lessons after work, although Shushkevich was not allowed to be alone with him, as a colleague, Rubenchik, had to always be there, and he was not allowed to ask about Oswald's past or his coming to the USSR either.<ref name="mail" /><ref name="19november">{{cite news |title=Stanislau Shushkevich: 'I Never Saw Oswald Get Excited About Anything' |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/interview-transcript-oswald-shushkevich-belarus-soviet/25172632.html |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty |date=21 November 2013 |language=en}}</ref> Shushkevich later mentioned his connection with Oswald in July 1992, when he told an official of the Embassy of the US that he did not believe that Oswald was capable of the [[Assassination of John F. Kennedy]], which he was convicted of in 1963.<ref name="cia">{{cite document |date=13 July 1992 |title=CABLE: CHAIRMAN SHUSHKEVICH WAS LEE HARVEY OSWALD'S RUSSIAN TEACHER |location=Minsk |publisher=CIA |page=2}}</ref> This is confirmed by a [[CIA]] document, RIF #104-10014-10053, which was released as part of the John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Collection Act of 1992.<ref name="cia" /> Shushkevich would also later recall that during the investigation into Oswald, writer and journalist [[Norman Mailer]] visited him with a team asking for Oswald's personal file.<ref name="19november" /> Shushkevich got permission to release the file through Eduard Shirkovsky, the last chairman of the [[Committee for State Security of the Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic|KGB of the BSSR]].<ref name="19november" />

=== At MRTI (1966-1970) ===
After leaving the plant to complete his dissertation, which he did in 1963, Shushkevich was appointed [[prorector]] for research at the [[Belarusian State University of Informatics and Radioelectronics|Minsk Radioengineering Institute]] (MRTI) in 1966.<ref name="novy" /> He was appointed to the role after the rector of BSU, Anton Sevchenko, personally arranged this through the Minsk Party Committee.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=73}} While at MRTI, he became a candidate and later full member of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1968.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=75}} He also taught new courses there in [[quantum electronics]] and in physics, while also helping find work for the institute across Moscow and Leningrad.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=73-75}} However, he soon came into conflict with MRTI's rector, Ivan Kovalyov, and in early 1970 requested six months' leave.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=75-76}} In return, Shushkevich said that after the six months he would submit his doctoral dissertation, and then resign from the MRTI immediately.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=75-76}} On 13 May 1970, he defended his dissertation to achieve his [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree in Moscow, which was entitled "Informative Parameters of Signals", and thereafter he left MRTI and immediately returned to BSU.<ref name="novy" />

=== At BSU (1970-1990) ===
[[File:Belarus-Minsk-BSU-Rector's Office-2.jpg|thumb|left|Rector's Office of the [[Belarusian State University]]. Shushkevich worked for a long time at BSU prior to entering politics.]]
Upon returning to BSU, Shushkevich was appointed Head of the Department of Nuclear Physics. He was also later appointed a full [[professor]] in 1972. According to Shushkevich, he was appointed head of the department because Alexander Pisarevsky had recently left to return to Leningrad, and the candidate chosen by the rector did not last, which led him to become its acting head until he was promoted to full head by competition.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=77-79}}<ref name="novy" /> At BSU, his department was divided into three specialisations: nuclear physics, nuclear electronics, and nuclear power installation.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=79}} The latter, installations, was not taught physically at BSU but instead at the Institute of Nuclear Energy in [[Sosny, Minsk|Sosny]], because Sosny had a [[nuclear reactor]].{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=96-97}} Shushkevich got funding for the department through contracts across the USSR, including through joint expeditions with [[Moscow State University]] to [[Vladivostok]] and [[Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky]].{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=89-90}} Simultaneously, during Shushkevich's time with the department, he also worked as a foreign lecturer at the [[Jagiellonian University]], [[University of Jena]], and [[University of Ljubljana]].{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=14}} As a side job, he also co-wrote [[textbooks]], the most famous of which was entitled "Fundamentals of Radio Electronics", which he co-wrote with Mikhail Yefimchik.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=94}} It was later included in the recommendation list of the Ministry of Higher Education, and was what earned him the State Prize of the BSSR in 1986.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=94}} Shortly before the award, in 1985, while continuing to head the department, he was also made prorector for research at BSU after First Secretary [[Mikalay Slyonkow]] recommended him during a visit.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=93-94}}

=== Chernobyl disaster ===
[[File:Chernobylreactor 1.jpg|thumb|left|Reactor Building No. 4 of the [[Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant]] in 2006. In subsequent interviews, Shushkevich attributed the Soviet reaction to Chernobyl as the reason he entered politics.]]
Shortly after the [[Chernobyl disaster]] (or Chornobyl), Shushkevich opened up his laboratories to have items tested that were received from civilians for radioactivity.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=15}}<ref name="tut">{{cite news |title=Станислав Шушкевич показал свой Минск и рассказал, что считает своим «самым великим преступлением» |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801180541/https://news.tut.by/society/647466.html |access-date=26 October 2026 |work=Tut |date=1 August 2019}}</ref> He actively advertised the testing in newspapers in Minsk, which was noticed by the authorities. Shushkevich also agreed to join a state Byelorussian commission on the Chernobyl disaster, but was eventually dropped from it due to insisting that the data the commission collected be published publicly.<ref name="current">{{cite news |last1=Морозова |first1=Клара |title=Безъядерная Беларусь и пенсия в два доллара. Что нужно знать о первом лидере независимой Беларуси Станиславе Шушкевиче |url=https://www.currenttime.tv/a/stanislav-shushkevich/31834369.html?ysclid=mvn5krrc79125862071 |access-date=26 October 2026 |work=Настоящее Время |date=4 May 2022 |language=ru}}</ref> Shushkevich then attempted to write appeals to the Council of Ministers of the USSR and the Academy of Sciences, but was met with standard replies.<ref name="novy" /> Eventually, the first secretary of the party committee for Minsk, Bazkho, allegedly summoned Shushkevich to his offices and accused him of spreading panic due to his advertising, although Shushkevich denied this and said he would continue to do so since he was an expert on radioactivity.<ref name="novy" />

On either 14 or 15 May 1986, [[Mikhail Gorbachev]] gave a televised address about Chernobyl.<ref name="kp">{{cite news |title=Станислав Шушкевич: "Уговорил Кастро отпустить заключенных – и отдыхаю в Мексике бесплатно" |url=https://kp.ua/life/654157-stanyslav-shushkevych-uhovoryl-kastro-otpustyt-zakluichennykh-y-otdykhaui-v-meksyke-besplatno |access-date=26 October 2026 |work=KP.UA |date=5 December 2019 |language=ru}}</ref>{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=98}} Shushkevich later attributed the speech to what made him want to enter politics, as he strongly disliked that the speech gave no instructions about what to do, especially in the heavily affected Byelorussia, and he also found that parts of the speech were false.<ref name="tut" />{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=98-100}} In later interviews, Shushkevich also called the speech a "disgrace", and subsequently blamed Gorbachev for [[thyroid cancer]] that was present in children in Belarus, which he attributed to Chernobyl.<ref name="kp" /> Additionally, he said Gorbachev had put the party's interests ahead of the health of the children by not properly informing the public.{{sfn|Шушкевич|2012|p=100}}

== Communist Party career ==
=== Supreme Soviet ===
In 1989, Shushkevich finally entered politics.<ref>{{cite news |title=С одной стороны — Чернобыль, с другой — правда о Куропатах и независимость. Рассказываем о роли Горбачева в белорусской истории |url=https://news.zerkalo.io/cellar/21060.html?ysclid=mvnevf005c841895276#google_vignette |access-date=26 October 2026 |work=Зеркало |date=31 August 2022 |language=ru}}</ref> According to Shushkevich, he said that a group of friends from BSU had nominated him as a candidate for a people's deputy in the upcoming [[1989 Soviet Union legislative election]].<ref name="novy" /> He said that although he initially hesitated, he relented and approved his nomination.<ref name="novy" /> For his constituency, there were six other candidates, with Shushkevich being endorsed by the newly formed [[Belarusian Popular Front]] led by [[Zianon Pazniak]].<ref name="novy" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Prince |first1=Todd |title=Stanislau Shushkevich, First Leader Of Independent Belarus, Dead At 87 |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/shushkevich-obituary-belarus/31833591.html |access-date=26 October 2026 |work=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty |date=3 March 2023 |language=en}}</ref> During the election, leaflets claiming he was a [[KGB]] informant who had informed on his father started to circulate, which Shushkevich said was ordered by the district party committee.<ref name="novy" /> He eventually won the elections with a majority, and thus entered the parliament.<ref name="novy" />

== Presidency ==
When Supreme Soviet chairman [[Nikolai Dementey]] was ousted for his support of the [[1991 Soviet coup d'état attempt|August 1991 coup attempt]], Shushkevich became interim speaker,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.knowbysight.info/1_BELOR/03491.asp |title=Высшие органы государственной власти Белорусской ССР |access-date=29 June 2021 |archive-date=24 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024023825/http://www.knowbysight.info/1_BELOR/03491.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> and presided over Belarus voting to secede from the Soviet Union. He thus became the newly minted nation's first leader. On 18 September, Shushkevich was elected Chairman of the Supreme Soviet.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/892 |title=Беларусь свободна. Назло надменному соседу |date=23 September 1991 |access-date=16 July 2021 |archive-date=16 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716100339/https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/892 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:RIAN archive 52076 Leonid Kravchuk, Stanislav Shushkevich and Boris Yeltsin.jpg|thumb|left|Stanislav Shushkevich at the signing of the [[Belavezha Accords]] with [[Leonid Kravchuk]] and [[Boris Yeltsin]] in 1991]]
On 8 December 1991, in [[Belavezhskaya Pushcha]] and together with the leaders of Russia ([[Boris Yeltsin]]) and Ukraine ([[Leonid Kravchuk]]), he signed a declaration that the [[Soviet Union]] was dissolved and replaced by the [[Commonwealth of Independent States]]; the declaration later became known as the "[[Belovezh Accords]]".
[[File:Stanisłaŭ Šuškievič ja Toomas Hendrik Ilves.jpg|thumb|Shushkevich and [[President of Estonia]] [[Toomas Hendrik Ilves]] in 2011]]
Shushkevich had the vestigial Soviet nuclear arsenal (both tactical and strategic) withdrawn from Belarus, without preconditions or compensation from Russia or the West. However, other reforms became stalled due to the opposition from a hostile parliament as well as from Prime Minister [[Vyacheslav Kebich]].{{citation needed|date=August 2023}}
[[File:Stanisłau Szuszkiewicz - doctor honoris causa SGH 2.jpg|thumb|Shushkevich in Warsaw, Poland achieving Doctor Honoris Causa, 2014]]
In late 1993, [[Alexander Lukashenko]], the then-chairman of the anti-corruption committee of the Belarusian parliament, accused 70 senior government officials, including Shushkevich, of corruption, including stealing state funds for personal purposes. Lukashenko's accusations forced a [[vote of confidence]], which Shushkevich lost. Shushkevich was replaced by [[Vyacheslav Nikolayevich Kuznetsov|Vyacheslav Kuznetsov]] and later by [[Myechyslau Hryb]].{{citation needed|date=August 2023}}

== Post-presidency ==
At the [[1994 Belarusian presidential election]] (the first one after the secession from the Soviet Union), six candidates stood, including Lukashenko, Shushkevich and Kebich, with the latter regarded as the clear favorite. In the first round Lukashenko won 45% of the vote against 17% for Kebich, 13% for Paznyak and 10% for Shushkevich.

In 2002 Shushkevich sued the Belarusian Ministry of Labor and Social Security: due to inflation, his retirement pension as a former head of state was the equivalent of US$1.80 monthly.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.trud.ru/trud.php?id=200503030361101 |language=ru|script-title=ru:Как поживают экс-президенты стран СНГ |trans-title=Life of the Ex-presidents of CIS Countries |date=3 March 2005 |publisher=[[Trud (Russian newspaper)|Trud]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927224533/http://www.trud.ru/trud.php?id=200503030361101 |archive-date=27 September 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.svoboda.org/archive/ll_man/0302/ll.031102-1.asp |title=Stanislav Shushkevich |last1=Шарый |first1=Андрей |date=11 March 2002 |website=[[Radio Liberty]] |language=ru |access-date=20 July 2007 |archive-date=4 December 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081204182837/http://www.svoboda.org/archive/ll_man/0302/ll.031102-1.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> To earn income, Shushkevich lectured extensively in foreign universities including in [[Poland]], the [[United States]] and Asian countries.

In 2004 he attempted to [[2004 Belarusian parliamentary election|participate in parliamentary elections]], but was refused registration by the [[Election management body|electoral commission]].{{citation needed|date=August 2023}}

He continued to be active in politics,<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/jun/10/soviet-union-comeback|title=Back in the USSR: Belarusian leader who helped bury Soviet Union says it is making a comeback|last=Rice-Oxley|first=Mark|authorlink=Mark Rice-Oxley|date=10 June 2014|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=1 August 2019|language=en|archive-date=18 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190918031819/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/jun/10/soviet-union-comeback|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/interview-with-belaruss-first-president-stanislav_b_58f4c2c1e4b04cae050dc8fa|title=Interview with Belarus's First President Stanislav Shushkevich on Lukashenka's Rise and Belarus's Political Future|last=Ramani|first=Samuel|date=17 April 2017|website=HuffPost|language=en|access-date=1 August 2019|archive-date=29 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200329011941/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/interview-with-belaruss-first-president-stanislav_b_58f4c2c1e4b04cae050dc8fa|url-status=live}}</ref> heading the [[Belarusian Social Democratic Assembly]] party from 1998 until 2018.

Shushkevich also remained an outspoken critic of Lukashenko and his relationship with Russian President [[Vladimir Putin]], feeling Lukashenko had surrendered Belarusian independence and turned the country into a "fragment of Russia".<ref>{{cite news|last=Nevedomskaya|first=Tatyana|url=https://www.dw.com/ru/stanislav-shushkevich-lukashenko-sdal-belorusskuju-nezavisimost/a-60048715|title=Станислав Шушкевич: Лукашенко сдал белорусскую независимость|publisher=[[Deutsche Welle]]|date=8 December 2021|access-date=22 June 2026|language=ru}}</ref> He also described Belarus' [[cult of personality|cults of personality]] for both leaders by mentioning that "there was a cult in Soviet times, but there was a personality. Now, there is a cult but no personality."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.currenttime.tv/a/30347703.html|title="Есть культ, нет личности". Итоги десятилетия с первым руководителем независимой Беларуси Станиславом Шушкевичем|publisher=[[Current Time TV]]|date=31 December 2019|access-date=22 June 2026|language=ru}}</ref> He condemned the [[2014 Russian annexation of Crimea]] along with the ensuing [[war in Donbas]] and [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/ukrainian/news-61317837|title=Помер перший керівник незалежної Білорусі Станіслав Шушкевич|website=[[BBC News Ukrainian]]|publisher=[[BBC News]]|date=4 May 2022|access-date=22 June 2026|language=ua}}</ref>
[[File:Šuškievič bchd (cropped).jpg|thumb|Shushkevich in 2009]] 

In 2026, after his death,  the Belarusian authorities added Stanislav Shushkevich's book "Neocommunism in Belarus: Ideology, Practice, Perspectives" to the [[Classification of extremist materials in Belarus|list of extremist materials]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.svaboda.org/a/33802844.html|title=Улады прызналі «экстрэмісцкімі» мовазнаўчую кнігу Вінцука Вячоркі і зборнік цытатаў Алексіевіч|work=[[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]]|language=be-tarask}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He was married to his wife Irina from 1976 onward. According to him, she forced him to start a healthy lifestyle. They had a son named Stanislav and daughter named Elena.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Shakhnovich|first=Tatyana|title=Станислав Шушкевич: «Я до сих пор человек Ельцина, а с Кебичем помирюсь – если извинится!»|trans-title=Stanislav Shushkevich: "I'm still Yeltsin's man, and I'll make peace with Kebich – if he apologizes!"|date=2016-10-04|newspaper=[[Komsomolskaya Pravda]]|language=ru|url=https://www.kp.ru/daily/26316.3/3194152/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250129222756/https://www.kp.ru/daily/26316.3/3194152/|archive-date=2025-01-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Martinovich|first=Denis|title="Мой папа убил Михоэлса". Кем стали дети руководителей Беларуси|trans-title="My dad killed Mikhoels." Who are the children of the leaders of Belarus|date=2016-10-04|website=[[Tut.By]]|language=ru|url=https://news.tut.by/culture/514573.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191108070033/https://news.tut.by/culture/514573.html|archive-date=2019-11-08|access-date=2019-08-01}}</ref> Shushkevich was admitted to hospital and placed in an intensive care unit in April 2022, due to complications from [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=First Leader Of Independent Belarus, Stanislau Shushkevich, In Intensive Care|date=2022-04-26|website=[[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]]|url=https://www.rferl.org/a/belarus-shushkevich-intensive-care/31821748.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251008140530/https://www.rferl.org/a/belarus-shushkevich-intensive-care/31821748.html|archive-date=2025-10-08|access-date=2022-04-26}}</ref> 

== Death  ==
On 3 May 2022, it was reported that Shushkevich had died at the age of 87 in Minsk.<ref name="moscowtime">{{cite news |title=Ex-Belarus Leader Who Helped Dissolve Soviet Union Dies Aged 87 |url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/05/04/ex-belarus-leader-who-helped-dissolve-soviet-union-dies-aged-87-a77572 |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=The Moscow Times |date=4 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> His death was confirmed by his wife, Irina, according to the [[Voice of America]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Latest Developments in Ukraine: May 4 |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/latest-developments-in-ukraine-may-4/6556327.html |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=Voice of America |date=4 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> Shushkevich died of complications from [[COVID-19]], after having been in intensive care since April.<ref name="moscowtime" /> 

In a statement, the opposition leader of Belarus, [[Svetlana Tikhanovskaya]], called his death "a big loss".<ref>{{cite news |title=Ex-Belarus leader Stanislav Shushkevich, who helped dissolve USSR, dies at 87 |url=https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20220504-ex-belarus-leader-stanislav-shushkevich-who-helped-dissolve-ussr-dies-at-87 |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=France 24 |date=4 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> However, the Belarusian government under Lukashenko did not officially comment on his death, with the state news agency [[Belta]] simply releasing a chronology of his career.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Trevelyan |first1=Mark |title=Ex-Belarus leader Shushkevich, the man who sacked Gorbachev, dies at 87 |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/ex-belarus-leader-shushkevich-man-who-sacked-gorbachev-dies-87-2022-05-04/ |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=Reuters |date=4 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> Previously, Lukashenko had expressed his condolences to other Belarusian leaders, such as [[Nikolai Slyunkov]].<ref name="london" /> The Prime Minister of Lithuania, [[Ingrida Simonyte]], tweeted that he would be remembered for his help in dissolving the Soviet Union.<ref>{{cite news |title=Stanislav Shushkevich, post-Soviet leader of Belarus, dies |url=https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-covid-health-alexander-lukashenko-mikhail-gorbachev-05ede00701ca33210ce3b9dda65613ce |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=AP News |date=4 May 2022}}</ref>

Shortly after his death, Irina said she hoped that a [[state funeral]] would be held for him, but that nobody had contacted her.<ref name="moscowtime" /> Shushkevich's funeral ultimately took place on 7 May at the [[Cathedral of the Holy Name of Saint Virgin Mary]] on Freedom Square.<ref name="smart" /> Hundreds of people attended his funeral, alongside some journalists and diplomats.<ref>{{cite news |title=Сотни белорусов пришли проститься со Станиславом Шушкевичем |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220510174338/https://thinktanks.by/publication/2022/05/07/sotni-belorusov-prishli-prostitsya-so-stanislavom-shushkevichem.html |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=thinktanks.by |date=7 May 2022}}</ref> He was later beside his mother at the Northern Cemetery in Minsk.<ref name="smart">{{cite news |title=Прощание со Станиславом Шушкевичем прошло в Кафедральном соборе Пресвятой Девы Марии |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220510174343/https://smartpress.by/news/23044/ |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=SmartPress |date=7 May 2022}}</ref> Traditionally, Belarusian leaders and other famous people had been buried at the Eastern Cemetery in Minsk, with former diplomat Pavel Mastukevich arguing that Shushkevich had been buried elsewhere because of political reasons.<ref name="london">{{cite news |title=За государственный счет с увековечением памяти. Как хоронят руководителей Беларуси |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721132256/https://mediazona.by/article/2022/09/19/london-bridge-is-down |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=Медиазона Беларусь |date=19 September 2022 |language=ru}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==
* Honored Worker of Science and Technology of the BSSR (1982)<ref>{{cite book |title=Prafesary i daktary navuk Belaruskaha dzi︠a︡rz︠h︡aŭnaha universitėta, 1921-2001, 80 hod |date=2001 |publisher=BDU |isbn=978-985-445-542-6 |page=321 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Prafesary_i_daktary_navuk_Belaruskaha_dz/WaglAQAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=%C2%AB%D0%97%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BB%D1%83%D0%B6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BD%D1%8B%D0%B9+%D0%B4%D0%B5%D1%8F%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D1%8C+%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%83%D0%BA%D0%B8+%D0%B8+%D1%82%D0%B5%D1%85%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B8+%D0%91%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%83%D1%81%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B9+%D0%A1%D0%A1%D0%A0%C2%BB+%2B+%C2%AB%D0%A1%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B2+%D0%A8%D1%83%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87%C2%BB+1982&dq=%C2%AB%D0%97%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BB%D1%83%D0%B6%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BD%D1%8B%D0%B9+%D0%B4%D0%B5%D1%8F%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BB%D1%8C+%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%83%D0%BA%D0%B8+%D0%B8+%D1%82%D0%B5%D1%85%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%B8+%D0%91%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%83%D1%81%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B9+%D0%A1%D0%A1%D0%A0%C2%BB+%2B+%C2%AB%D0%A1%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B2+%D0%A8%D1%83%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87%C2%BB+1982&printsec=frontcover |access-date=25 October 2026 |language=ru}}</ref>
* [[Prize of the Council of Ministers of the USSR]] (1985)<ref>{{cite book |title=Kto estʹ kto v Belarusi |date=2001 |publisher=Knizhnyĭ dom "Universitet" |isbn=978-985-6544-16-6 |page=308 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Kto_est%CA%B9_kto_v_Belarusi/mpcrAQAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=%C2%AB%D0%9F%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%83%D0%BC+%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D0%B0+%D0%9C%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2+%D0%A1%D0%A1%D0%A1%D0%A0%C2%BB+%2B+%C2%AB%D0%A1%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B2+%D0%A8%D1%83%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87%C2%BB+1985&dq=%C2%AB%D0%9F%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%83%D0%BC+%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D0%B0+%D0%9C%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2+%D0%A1%D0%A1%D0%A1%D0%A0%C2%BB+%2B+%C2%AB%D0%A1%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B2+%D0%A8%D1%83%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87%C2%BB+1985&printsec=frontcover |access-date=25 October 2026 |language=ru}}</ref>
* State Prize of the BSSR (1988)<ref>{{cite book |last1=Кильчевский |first1=А. |last2=Гусаков |first2=Владимир |last3=Азаренко |first3=Владимир |title=Национальная академия наук Беларуси |date=23 March 2018 |publisher=ИД “Белорусская наука” |isbn=978-5-04-107419-7 |page=589 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/%D0%9D%D0%B0%D1%86%D0%B8%D0%BE%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%BB%D1%8C%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D0%B0%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B8/OQNTDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%C2%AB%D0%93%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%83%D0%B4%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B2%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BD%D0%B0%D1%8F+%D0%BF%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%8F+%D0%91%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%83%D1%81%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B9+%D0%A1%D0%A1%D0%A0%C2%BB+%2B+%C2%AB%D0%A1%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B2+%D0%A8%D1%83%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87%C2%BB+1988&pg=PA589&printsec=frontcover |access-date=25 October 2026 |language=ru}}</ref>
* Corresponding Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus]] (1991)<ref>{{cite news |title=Учил Освальда, подписывал Беловежские соглашения: чем запомнился Шушкевич |url=https://tochka.by/articles/policy/uchil_osvalda_podpisyval_belovezhskie_soglasheniya_chem_zapomnilsya_shushkevich/?ysclid=mvn46e6oj7928403035 |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=tochka.by |date=15 December 2024 |language=ru}}</ref>
* Pylyp Orlyk International Ukrainian Prize (by the Pylyp Orlyk Foundation, 1997)<ref>{{cite news |title=Белорусы в смятении: утром людям сообщили о кончине первого президента - подробности |url=https://kyiv.ukrainianwall.com/ru/88587-bilorusi-v-sum-yatti-vranci-lyudyam-povidomili-pro-smert-pershogo-prezidenta-podrobici |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=Ukrainian Wall |date=4 May 2022 |language=ru}}</ref>
